text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The opposition United Democratic Forces candidate Petar Stoyanov took the lead in the first round of Sunday's presidential elections with 44.9 percent of the vote. The Socialist candidate Ivan Marazov came second with 26.9 percent and the Bulgarian Business bloc candidate George Ganchev came third with 21.6 percent, according to preliminary results of the Central Electoral Committee.

-- Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov forecast annual inflation of some 33 percent for 1997 as a result of a projected decline in the budget deficit and sales of Bulgarian treasury bills in the international markets.

-- Representatives of private Russian corporation NITEK are expected to discuss with the Privatisation Agency director Vesselin Blagoev today the possible privatisation of the state pharmaceutical producer Sopharma, privatisation agency sources said.

-- The government agriculture fund will extend a credit line for advance payments by trade companies appointed by the minister of agriculture to grains producers at the price of 35,000 levs for a tonne of wheat harvested in 1997. In addition the producers will have to sow at least 3.5 hectares for every contracted tonne of grains, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Commercial banks decreased their losses from 32.8 billion levs at the end of 1995 to 21.1 billion levs for the first six months of 1996, the central bank's half-yearly report said.

-- Some one million hectares of land has been sown with grain and the sown areas are expected to reach 1.2-1.3 million hectares if the weather holds, the head of the crop production department, Georgi Spiridonov, said.

-- The European Investment Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development are expected to extend some $150 million to integrate Bulgaria with the European energy system and the reconstruct the Maritza Iztok-3 coal-fired power station, Energy Minister Rumen Ovcharov said.
-- Construction companies posted pre-tax profit of about 40 million levs for the first six months, the first positive financial result in the sector for several years, the construction ministry said.
